title: fix(lint): one-line fix lines for 17 more author-time rule ids (slice 15); `os explain RULE_ID` carries what they explained
body:
Part of #22161
Clause-②: no

Stage 2 of the card, slice 15: the over-long `fix:` lines, continued in slices 11 to 14's shape. Each finding's `hint` (the CLI's `fix:` line, the runtime issue's `hint`) of 17 more `packages/lint` rule ids, in eight rule files, is now one remedy line of at most 200 characters, and what the lines used to explain is each id's `RULE_EXPLANATIONS` entry behind `os explain RULE_ID`. The card stays open: 41 author-time ids still carry a hint over 200 characters (the last section).

## What changes

- **One remedy line per finding.** The 17 ids, every hint the lint suite fires, before → after (count of distinct hints · length range):

| rule id | file | lint suite, before → after | runtime door |
|---|---|---|---|
| `react-chart-field-unprovisioned` | `validate-react-page-props.ts` | 1 · 362 → 1 · 175 | CLI only |
| `react-prop-missing-required` | same | 2 · 71–277 → 3 · 55–131 | CLI only |
| `react-page-source-unparseable` | same | 1 · 254 → 1 · 105 | CLI only |
| `react-block-needs-record-context` | same | 5 · 138–228 → 5 · 105–195 | CLI only |
| `action-body-write-unprovisioned-anchor` | `validate-action-body-writes.ts` | 1 · 358 → 1 · 171 | CLI only |
| `action-body-write-unknown-field` | same | 9 · 283–323 → 10 · 51–91 | CLI only |
| `action-record-write-discarded` | same | 3 · 307–309 → 3 · 102–104 | CLI only |
| `action-body-source-unparseable` | same | 1 · 254 → 1 · 105 | CLI only |
| `agent-authoring-withdrawn` | `validate-ai-agent-authoring.ts` | 7 · 79–363 → 7 · 79–158 | CLI only |
| `default-agent-outside-roster` | same | 1 · 237 → 1 · 118 | CLI only |
| `flow-node-write-unprovisioned-anchor` | `validate-flow-node-writes.ts` | 1 · 358 → 1 · 171 | `flow` write, 2xx advisory |
| `flow-node-write-unknown-field` | same | 14 · 233–289 → 15 · 54–110 | `flow` write, 422 |
| `validation-rule-json-schema-uncompilable` | `validate-rule-compilability.ts` | 1 · 341 → 1 · 124 | `object` write, 422 |
| `validation-rule-regex-uncompilable` | same | 5 · 287–300 → 5 · 122–135 | `object` write, 422 |
| `translation-section-name-missing` | `validate-translatable-sections.ts` | 9 · 335–359 → 9 · 148–172 | CLI only |
| `object/managed-api-method-unaffordable` | `validate-managed-api-methods.ts` | 7 · 313–357 → 8 · 110–169 | `object` write, 422 |
| `nav-object-unservable` | `validate-nav-object-servability.ts` | 3 · 342–348 → 3 · 150–156 | CLI only |

A count that rises is a case this slice added (a far-miss unknown field on the action and flow rules, every write verb on the managed-object rule, a third required binding fired from the contract).

- **The reasoning moves, the remedy stays.**
  - The three anchor ids (`react-chart-field-unprovisioned`, `action-body-write-unprovisioned-anchor`, `flow-node-write-unprovisioned-anchor`) print `unprovisionedAnchorFix()`, slice 14's one-line form: the three ways out in one line. How (`columnMap`, `ownership: 'none'`, `systemFields: { audit: false }`) is the shared `UNPROVISIONED_ANCHOR_REMEDY` paragraph, now in their three entries too.
  - The two parse ids (`react-page-source-unparseable`, `action-body-source-unparseable`) print `PARSE_FAILURE_FIX`. What a partially recovered tree leaves unchecked was already their entries'.
  - `action-body-write-unknown-field` prints the hook sibling's line. Which shapes `ACTION_BODY_WRITE_PATTERNS` checks, why `ctx.input` is not one, and that the warning never blocks a build are a new paragraph of its entry. `action-record-write-discarded` keeps the `updateById` remedy; why only a provably dead write is reported was already the entry's, and "never blocks a build" joins it.
  - `flow-node-write-unknown-field`: why it gates where the body rules advise was already the entry's.
  - The two agent ids: that skills attach to `ask` / `build` by `surface` affinity is one shared paragraph, `SKILLS_ATTACH_BY_SURFACE`, in both entries. The withdrawn-agent entry also says why dropping the persona loses nothing. The line keeps the count of referenced skills, now in the singular for one.
  - The two compile ids: the escaped regex spellings and the named `format`s, and the shapes `type` / `required` / `$ref` take, are new paragraphs. The regex line still quotes the source.
  - `translation-section-name-missing`: that the suggested name is never a key derived from the label is the explanation's.
  - `object/managed-api-method-unaffordable`: removal first, then the affordance "once a guard enforces the write". The ADR-0092 D4 condition was already the entry's.
  - `nav-object-unservable`: the line keeps "unless it is API-disabled on purpose". The credential-material reason was already the entry's.
- **Two lines come from the spec's text, and stay there.**
  - `react-block-needs-record-context` prints the spec's replacement for the block (`REACT_RECORD_BLOCK_ALTERNATIVES`) behind the lead-in `Instead:`, where it used to say `On a react page bind the record yourself:`. That the replacement binds the record itself is a new paragraph of the entry. The longest, `record:related_list`'s, is 195.
  - `react-prop-missing-required` quotes the contract's description of the missing binding, now its first sentence. That sentence names the binding and its spelling (`Pass data={…}: The object this block binds to, written as the metadata-tier data source: data={{ provider: 'object', object: '…' }}`). The cut is the one `schemaRefusalHead` makes for a forwarded spec refusal. The rest of `ListView.data`'s description (which providers are accepted, why the prop is required) is the contract's, and the published react-blocks reference carries it whole.
  - New pins hold both to the bound across the spec's whole table. Every `REACT_RECORD_BLOCK_ALTERNATIVES` entry and every required binding in `REACT_BLOCKS` is fired and held to 200. A spec edit that grows one past it turns the rule's test red.
- **Nothing else moves.**
  - Every `message`, rule id, severity and `path` is unchanged, and so is what each rule accepts or refuses.
  - Every hunk in the eight rule files is a `hint` expression, a comment, an import swapped to a shared short form, or `descriptionHead()`.
  - No condition, branch, skip or dedupe moved, and no name is added to or removed from a published entry.
- `.changeset/22161-lint-slice-15-one-line-fix.md`: `@objectstack/lint` `patch`, `Clause-②: no`, with the runtime `hint` FROM → TO for every id that fires at the runtime gate.

### File surface: the claim's

The claim (`6133662163`) names the eight rule files, `rule-explanations.ts`, the shared one-line producers where an id converges on them, a text-only test rider and the changeset.
- The edits stay inside it. `system-fields.ts` and `checked-parse.ts` needed no edit: the ids converge on slice 14's `unprovisionedAnchorFix()` and `PARSE_FAILURE_FIX` as they are.
- `packages/cli` and `packages/metadata-protocol` needed no rider: no entry was added, and no test there reads these hints' text.
- After this slice `unprovisionedAnchorHint()` keeps three callers (`validate-widget-bindings.ts`, `validate-flow-template-paths.ts`, `validate-page-field-bindings.ts`). `PARSE_FAILURE_HINT` keeps one (`lint-startup-registry-verdict.ts`).

## The runtime wire

Measured at the door with `runRuntimeAuthoringRules`, on the base dist and on the rebuilt one: a scratch probe of 19 writes across `object`, `flow`, `action`, `page`, `app`, `agent` and `view`.

- an `object` write:
  - `object/managed-api-method-unaffordable` (422 `issues[].hint`): two refused verbs / every write verb, 335 / 372 → 132 / 169;
  - `validation-rule-regex-uncompilable` (422): the pattern `([` / a 28-character pattern, 288 / 314 → 123 / 149;
  - `validation-rule-json-schema-uncompilable` (422): 341 → 124.
- a `flow` write:
  - `flow-node-write-unknown-field` (422): with / without a near miss, 271 / 250 → 92 / 71;
  - `flow-node-write-unprovisioned-anchor` (2xx `advisories[].hint`): 361 → 174.
- No write reaches the other twelve.
  - The four react-page ids, the four action-body ids, the two agent ids, `translation-section-name-missing` and `nav-object-unservable` are reference-suite members on the frozen `flow` default. A flow snapshot carries none of the collections they read.
  - The action, page, app, agent and view writes in the probe drew no finding at all.

Readers of `hint`, read-only against objectui `main` at `1fb1ced3` (the local `origin/main`, equal to the remote's; `git grep` for `.hint` reads, nothing fetched):
- Studio's `saveAdvisoryToast.ts` `formatFinding` renders `[rule] where — message hint` for every 2xx advisory, so the flow-node anchor toast shortens.
- `DraftChangesPanel.tsx` reads `hint` only for its in-browser security-posture pass (none of these ids).
- No objectui source reads a 422 issue's `hint`.
- REST (`PUT /api/v1/meta`) forwards `issues` / `advisories` as JSON (`toIssue` copies `hint` verbatim). `packages/mcp` registers no metadata write tool, so an MCP or AI author reaches the gate through REST.
- **No reader in either repository matches on `hint` text.** `check:watch-hint-literal` guards something else of the same name and ran in the gate set.

## Census (taken first, before any edit, at the base `abf86554c`)

Method: the earlier slices' scratch preload (`NODE_OPTIONS=--import`, never committed). It patches `Array.prototype.push` to record every finding-shaped object, deduped by (rule, hint) per process, with its push site. Lengths are the `hint` alone.

- **`packages/lint` suite**: the 17 ids re-measured at the base equal the claim's lengths exactly (362, 277, 254, 228, 358, 323, 309, 254, 363, 237, 358, 289, 341, 300, 359, 357, 348).
  - Base: 240 ids fire, 82 over 200 = 21 fenced + 3 repo-gate + 58 author-time. The 58 are slice 14's remaining list, id for id.
  - After, at `c6f65c38a`: 240 ids fire, 65 over 200 = 21 fenced + 3 repo-gate + 41 author-time, and every hint of the 17 is at most 200 (the table). The 41 are the 58 less these 17.
- **Runtime publish gate**, the whole `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` suite (which reads `@objectstack/lint` from source), in a base worktree and at the branch: `validation-rule-json-schema-uncompilable` 341 → 124 at the door, and none of the other 16 fires there. Test Files 228 passed, 3 skipped (231), Tests 28,224 passed, 19 skipped, in both.
- **`packages/cli` unit tier**, base worktree and branch: `agent-authoring-withdrawn` (its zero-skill arm) 196 → 112, and none of the other 16 fires there. Test Files 285 passed (285), Tests 4,280 passed (4,280), in both.
- **`os validate`** (the built CLI) on `app-crm`, `app-todo`, `app-showcase` and `app-multi-package`, base worktree and branch:
  - exit 0 each, and none of the 17 fires;
  - each prints the same 9 / 7 / 70 / 3 `rule:` lines;
  - the output is byte-identical once the worktree path and the millisecond timings (`Load time`, `Validation passed (…ms)`) are normalised. Those are the only differing lines.

## Tests

Every heavy run went through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` (slots `issue-22161-s15`, `issue-22161-s15-base`). Its VERDICT lines are in the report.

- **Each rule's own suite pins the new shape.** Each of the eight test files gains a last block. It holds every recorded `fix:` line of its converted ids to one line of at most 200 characters, behind a coverage control naming each arm:
  - the unknown-field lines with and without a suggestion (a far-miss case added on the action and flow rules);
  - both agent arms, with no, one and several referenced skills;
  - one, several and every refused verb;
  - both nav arms;
  - a record block with a named replacement and with the generic advice.

  A check per id then asserts that `explainRule(id)` holds what the line stopped saying. Seven recorders now keep `hint` beside `message`.
- **Moved pins.** Pins that read the old hint text moved to the explanation, text-only: the section rule's "never a key derived from the label", and the managed-object rule's `ADR-0092 D4`. The agent rule's zero-skills negative now names the new wording.
- **New pins hold an explanation's spelled-out list to its source**: the named regex formats to `FormatValidationSchema`'s `format` enum, and the JSON Schema primitive types.
- **Lint suite** at `c6f65c38a`: Test Files 137 passed (137), Tests 6,646 passed (6,646); VERDICT command-exit 0. At the base: Test Files 137 passed (137), Tests 6,614 passed (6,614).
- **Lint build and typecheck** at `c6f65c38a`: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm turbo run build --filter=@objectstack/lint...` (lint's build script runs `check-dts-emitted`) and `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint run typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit` + `check:test-typecheck` OK: 2 files / 6 errors / 2 pinned signatures held), VERDICT command-exit 0 each. The rebuilt dist carries the new text: `Instead: `, `once a guard enforces the write` and `author skills instead` have 1 hit each in `index.js` and `runtime.js`, and the new agent paragraph's text is in `index.js` and `rule-explanations.js`. The old lines are gone: `On a react page bind the record yourself`, `Do NOT open the API on an object` and `This gates the build rather than warning: the key is literal` have 0 hits in all three.
- **The built entries' export closure is unchanged** (the `Clause-②` check): the runtime export keys and the declaration exports of `index`, `runtime` and `rule-explanations` are identical, read from the base dist (`abf86554c`) and from the branch's rebuilt dist (`5aaa606c9`): 371 / 553, 6 / 11 and 2 / 3 names, 0 added and 0 removed. Read again at the final head against a `main` dist (`21c86444e`): the same counts, 0 added and 0 removed.
- **CLI unit tier** and **metadata-protocol suite**: measured before the merge, at `5aaa606c9`, against a base worktree at `abf86554c`, VERDICT command-exit 0 for all four runs. CLI unit tier: Test Files 285 passed (285), Tests 4,280 passed (4,280), in both. metadata-protocol: Test Files 228 passed, 3 skipped (231), Tests 28,224 passed, 19 skipped, in both. Not rerun after the merge: `main` brought no `packages/lint` file, and the final lint census equals the pre-merge one id for id.
- **Ablation**: one-shot, from the committed head `5aaa606c9`, through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` under the lock, with a shell `trap` restoring `HEAD` by absolute path. The rule suite imports the rule source, so there is no dist leg.
  - Mutation: `flow-node-write-unknown-field`'s pre-slice caveat ("This gates the build rather than warning: …") restored in `fixHint()`.
  - Predicted before the run: exactly the two new slice-15 cases in `validate-flow-node-writes.test.ts` go red, and every other case stays green.
  - Observed: Tests 2 failed, 42 passed (44), exactly those two, printing the old line.
  - The mutation landed (anchor x1 → x0, replacement x0 → x1, blob `084b6a3acbae` → `e2b288d993f2`) and was restored (blob `084b6a3acbae` == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty, `git status --porcelain` empty). The rule file and its test have the same blobs at the final head.
- **ESLint, narrowed**: `npx eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 17 changed `.ts` files at `c6f65c38a`: 17 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings.
  - The population is `eslint.config.mjs`'s `**/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts,js,jsx,mjs,cjs}` block plus its `packages/**` blocks.
  - The config never enables type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`), so no untouched file's verdict can move.
  - A control-character scan of every changed file found no match.
- **Gates**: one merge of `origin/main` through `scripts/pm/os-regen-merge.sh` (`5aaa606c9` → `c6f65c38a`, onto `21c86444e`). No conflict, and the branch edits no generated artifact. `main` brought `packages/spec`, `packages/cli` and `packages/metadata-protocol` changes and no `packages/lint` file.
  - `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, with no paths, at `c6f65c38a` (18 paths vs the merge base `21c86444e`) derived 62 commands.
  - 61 ran, each exit code captured before any pipe, all 0. The longest: `check:query-options-erasure` 290s, `check:slot-lookup` 151s, `check-comment-mask-corpus` 112s.
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` first refused (exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET: six packages had no dist). After building those six with their closure under the lock (VERDICT command-exit 0) it ran, exit 0 (107 entry points across 66 packages).
  - NOT MEASURED, by the dispatch's order: `check:type-check-debt`.
  - `--ran`: `62 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 61 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED`.
  - `origin/main` moved five commits after the merge (`240890cfb` … `e9e10fdab`), touching no `packages/lint` file; not merged again.
  - The artifact-roster and PR-context families are CI's.

## Acceptance notes

- **A long name can still lengthen a line.** The bound holds on every variant the suites, the runtime probe and the four example apps fire. The names in a hint are the author's: the object and field of the anchor lines, the section heading's slug (twice), the regex source, the nav target. The closest measured case is `react-block-needs-record-context` at 195 (a fixed spec string, `record:related_list`'s replacement). After it comes `translation-section-name-missing` at 172 (`showcase_contact` / `who_is_this`).
- **`react-prop-missing-required` still has no `os explain` entry.** An entry is keyed to a rule id constant the root barrel exports, and this id has none: it is a literal in `validate-react-page-props.ts`. Exporting one would add a name to `@objectstack/lint`'s published entry, which is `Clause-②: yes`, against this claim's `no`. So the route's "an id without an entry gains one" is not applied here. What its line stopped quoting is the contract's own text, which the published react-blocks reference keeps whole.
- **A record block's line keeps the spec's sentence verbatim**, a trailing period included. `record:related_list`'s replacement is 186 characters on its own, so the lead-in is a word. If the spec's table grows past the bound, the new pin turns red rather than printing a second line.
- **The long forms stay for their other callers.** `unprovisionedAnchorHint()` keeps three ids outside this slice and `PARSE_FAILURE_HINT` one (a repo-gate id). Each converges on the short form when its slice comes.
- **A docs transcript predates this card.** `content/docs/ui/react-pages.mdx` quotes an `os validate` transcript of `react-block-needs-record-context` whose verdict and `fix:` line are both pre-#22161 wording. The verdict changed in an earlier slice. It is a hand-written example, and `check:docs-transcript-drift` compares only the registry-derived numbers in a transcript, never finding text. No code path consumes it. Carrier: none named; noted, not filed.
